assignments.node_text: שִׂמְחָה שֶׁל מִצְוָה, כְּגוֹן חֲתֻנָּה שֶׁל מִצְוָה אוֹ שְׁאָר מִצְוָה בְּשִׂמְחָה
assignments.rationale: Joy of mitzvah is the teaching's primary eitza-instrument — the practical means through which confession becomes possible. Its essential nature is simchah (joy) rooted in mitzvah-performance. It does not share the nature of any existing package: not humble identity (Pkg 1), not royal will/glory (Pkg 2), not intellectual consciousness (Pkg 3). It belongs to the domain of holy joy — a distinct spiritual category in this Torah that serves as the engine of the entire causal chain.

Abundant mitzvot share the same essential nature as simchah shel mitzvah — they are the concrete content of mitzvah-joy. The text states 'שורש נקודות כל המצוות היא השמחה' — the root-point of all mitzvot IS joy. Mitzvot and simchah are described as structurally identical (each mitzvah = a limb of the stature of joy). This node belongs in the same joy/mitzvah domain.

Ribbuy ha-mitzvot (abundance of mitzvot) is semantically equivalent to mitzvot rabot — both denote the multiplicity of commandments whose root is joy. The text uses both terms interchangeably to describe how the accumulated light of mitzvah-joy overwhelms the obstacles of sin. Same essential nature as the joy/mitzvah domain.

assignments.node_id: שיעבר בכל השמחה, הינו בכל הקומה שיש בהשמחה
assignments.node_text: שֶׁיַּעֲבֹר בְּכָל הַשִּׂמְחָה, הַיְנוּ בְּכָל הַקּוֹמָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּהַשִּׂמְחָה
assignments.rationale: Traversing the full stature of joy (from feet to head, through all 248 limbs and 365 sinews) is the complete realization of simchah. The text describes joy as a 'komah shleimah' — a full spiritual stature. This node represents the fullness of simchah and belongs to the joy/mitzvah domain by essential nature.

assignments.node_id: נתבטל הדאגה של החטא המונעת השמחה
assignments.node_text: נִתְבַּטֵּל הַדְּאָגָה שֶׁל הַחֵטְא הַמּוֹנַעַת הַשִּׂמְחָה
assignments.rationale: The nullification of sin-worry is the clearing of obstacles TO joy. Its essential nature is the negative space of simchah — da'agah (worry) is defined in the text as 'the opposite of simchah' (היפך השמחה), and its nullification is the restoration of simchah. This node belongs to the joy domain because its entire identity is defined relative to simchah — it is the removal of what blocks joy, not an independent concept. The polarity is good because it describes the positive outcome of sin-worry being overcome.

Verbal confession (viduy devarim) belongs to the domain of speech/dibbur — the world of articulated word. The text explicitly links it: 'על ידי וידוי דברים נתתקן עולם הדבור' and explains that confession must be specifically 'in words' (בדיבורים דוקא) because the nefesh IS dibbur. Its essential nature is holy speech — the act of building and repairing the faculty of dibbur. This is distinct from joy (Pkg 4), from humble identity (Pkg 1), from royal will (Pkg 2), and from intellectual consciousness (Pkg 3).

The repair of the world of speech (olam ha-dibbur) shares the same essential nature as viduy devarim — both are expressions of the dibbur/speech domain. The text presents them as cause and effect (viduy → repair of dibbur), but within the package-assignment framework, both nodes are identified by their essential nature: the dimension of holy speech. The 'world of speech' is the domain-concept that viduy operates within.

The repair and building of speech (she-nitkan ve-nivneh ha-dibbur) is semantically equivalent to 'nitaken olam ha-dibbur' — both describe the same outcome: the restoration of the speech faculty. Same essential nature as the dibbur/speech domain.

assignments.node_text: נַעֲשֶׂה יִחוּד קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּהּ
assignments.rationale: The unification of the Holy One and Shekhinah is described in the text as the direct result of repairing dibbur: 'על-ידי שנתקן ונבנה הדבור... נעשה יחוד קודשא בריך הוא ושכינתה, שנתעורר הקול דלעלא ונתיחד עם הדבור.' The yichud is specifically the union of kol (voice from above) WITH dibbur (speech from below). Its essential nature is the consummation of the dibbur domain — voice uniting with speech. The text frames yichud not as an independent category but as the fulfilled state of the dibbur dimension, where the arousal from below (building speech) draws down the voice from above. It therefore belongs to the speech/dibbur package.

new_packages.label: שִׂמְחָה וּמִצְווֹת
new_packages.reason: These five nodes all share the essential nature of holy joy (simchah) rooted in mitzvah-performance. The Torah teaches that joy is a 'komah shleimah' (full stature) of 248 limbs and 365 sinews, each corresponding to a mitzvah. The root-point (shoresh nekudot) of all mitzvot IS simchah. The nullification of sin-worry is defined as the removal of the barrier to this same simchah. All five nodes operate within the single domain of mitzvah-generated joy that enables confession.

new_packages.label: דִּבּוּר וְוִדּוּי
new_packages.reason: These four nodes all share the essential nature of the dibbur (speech) domain. Viduy devarim is confession specifically through speech; the repair of olam ha-dibbur and the building of dibbur are the restoration of the speech faculty; and the yichud of HKB"H and Shekhinah is explicitly the union of kol (voice) with dibbur (speech) — the consummation of the speech dimension. The Torah ties the nefesh itself to dibbur ('nafshi yatz'ah be-dabro'), making this domain the soul-speech nexus where sin is repaired and divine unity achieved.

stats.note: All 9 cause/effect nodes were unassigned — none appeared in the 3 existing bechina-based packages. None could be assigned to existing packages by essential nature: the existing packages cover humble identity (Pkg 1: heel/Jacob/dal), royal will (Pkg 2: malkhut/kavod/ratzon), and intellectual consciousness (Pkg 3: rosh/mochin). The CE nodes belong to two distinct domains not represented in the existing packages: (1) holy joy generated by mitzvot, and (2) speech/confession leading to divine unity. Two new packages were therefore created. The Torah's full causal flow is now: Pkg 4 (joy/mitzvot) →eitza→ Pkg 5 (speech/confession) →eitza→ achieved through Pkg 3 (mochin/rosh), all in service of Pkg 2 (malkhut/ratzon) as expressed in Kaddish, built upon Pkg 1 (humble identity of Jacob/heel/dal).
